svg.aria-label: How to write 爱: 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing 爱
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 爱 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 爱.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E7%88%B1.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 爱, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the top: a flat left-falling stroke from the right, two dots, then a short left-falling stroke. Medians 5–6 draw the cover as 写 opens: a short left stroke, then a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting. Medians 7–10 draw the bottom: a horizontal, a long left-falling stroke from above it, then 又: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, and a right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
svg.text: How it is written — 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 10 movements

This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
